cache replacement: growing a value counts its replacement once and evicts the oldest other value

staticChecks.finding: Set and controlled lookup remeasure string UTF8 weights; sweep removes unusable/stale/rollback/overflow entries. Admission refuses >8MiB entries, subtracts a replaced value once, evicts oldest until size<=32 and retained text<=8MiB.
Controlled lookup/admission promotes by delete/set order; ordinary Map reads retain inspection semantics. Both byte/cardinality eviction are deterministic.
Finite numeric now/at only; finite nonnegative age<600000 for hits. TTL equality, rollback/nonfinite and invalid-cache metadata are refused.

Native errors never admit text; malformed cache-hit deletion remains same-object guarded. New successful validated results survive late malformed/HTTP/abort/read failure paths in the written native fixtures.

Delivered bounded response reader, request15s transport scope,4MiB byte admission, all six schemas/metadata/instructions/result bodies and package/lock/workflow/site/archive paths retain base Git identities.

independentNegativeReasoning: Exact8MiB entry has no empty-cache eviction loop;8MiB+1 admission is null-weight/refused. Replacement count is reduced once before admission; empty0byte text still consumes an entry.
Finite clock subtraction overflow is null-weight, and stale/unrelated future entries cannot bypass sweep before controlled hits.
Pending failed native fetch cannot delete a later admitted successful object; malformed-hit rejection compares original identity before deletion.
limits: STATIC source/control-flow review and Git metadata/declared SHA inheritance, no imports or tests/network/Node/job/execution. Current CI gate remains separate.

Supported injected plain mutable cache-entry fields are remeasured at controlled operations. Map.prototype bypass, replacement cache, accessors/mutation during operation are explicitly outside the fixture contract.
Retained UTF8 text8MiB/32entries per session is not process memory, JS/object/key overhead, parsed/output allocation, number of sessions or hard walltime.
Successful concurrent source revisions retain completion-order cache behavior; no remote-source freshness/rights/hosted latency/adoption/indexing outcome is established.
